title.en: What is energy? Light, sound, heat and movement

text.en: In a kitchen, food gets cooked, lights glow, a mixer makes a sound and the fridge keeps things cool. What makes all this happen?

Around us things move, light up, make sounds or get warmer or cooler. Something makes this happen and we call it energy.
Energy is what makes things move, light up, produce sound, do work and change temperature.
Activity: blow up a balloon, hold it tight and let go. The air rushing out pushes the balloon forward. For the balloon air rocket, tape the balloon to a straw on a string and watch it run along the string.
Rubber band guitar: stretch rubber bands over a box with a hole. When you pluck them they vibrate and make sound. This is sound energy. Thinner and thicker bands sound different.
Sun-powered water warmer: leave one cup of water in sunlight and another in shade for 15 to 20 minutes. The sunlit water is warmer. Sunlight gives us heat energy.
In parts of Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Ladakh, people keep cattle on the ground floor so the animals' heat keeps the family warm upstairs in winter.
The flying snake of Indian forests glides through the air by flattening its body, which shows activity in nature.
Bhadla Solar Park in Rajasthan is one of the largest solar power plants in the world.

problem.en: What did the balloon activity show?

text.en: Air rushes out of the balloon.
The balloon moves forward.
So moving air gives energy.

prompt.en: What is energy? Give two examples of what it can do.

requiredIdeas.en: Makes things move, light up, make sound, heat or cool

points.en: Energy makes things move, glow, sound and heat.
The Sun gives light and heat.
